contexts.text: Lot made a feast for them = dwelling together.
That good and truth would not dwell together with evil and falsity. Signified.
They who are in love to the Lord, dwell together with the Lord in good and truth. Signified.
The good of charity, in which there is the cohabitation of the Lord with man.

They thus dwell together not only in each thing, but also in the inmost things of life... They who, in the life of the body, have lived in such marriage love, are together and dwell together in Heaven as Angels; sometimes, also, with their children.
Of those who are in the good of truth is predicated dwelling together, which is signified by a feast.

This time my man will dwell together with me (), in the supreme sense, = the Divine Itself of the Lord and His Divine Human; in the internal sense, the heavenly marriage; and in the external sense, marriage love. Explained.
This union (of the Divine Itself and the Divine Human) is not dwelling together, but is expressed by dwelling together in the sense of the letter.
Zebulon = the dwelling together of good and truth... It is said the dwelling together of good and truth, because, in the Original Language, Zebulon means dwelling together.
To dwell together = to be together in good.
Under Dwell, see this reference.
This is called in Heaven cohabitation...
The delight is turned into undelight after a brief cohabitation.
[Swedenborg footnote 1.]. That husband and wife... dwell together in the inmost of life. References.
Men do not know with what Angels and Spirits they dwell together.

Zebulon was named from dwelling together; and dwelling together is said of married partners whose minds are conjoined as into a one; for this conjunction is spiritual dwelling together... There is dwelling together (with the Lord) when the man of the Church receives good from the Lord in truths... AE 447.
The reason no other married partners are received in Heaven, is that no others can dwell together there, that is, be together in one house, chamber, and bed.
This adjunction may be called spiritual dwelling together, which exists with married partners who tenderly love each other, however far apart they may be as to the body.
That with those who are in love truly conjugial, the happiness of dwelling together increases; but with those who are not in love truly conjugial, it decreases.
The reason a spiritual man thus dwells together with a natural man... CL 281:2.
As to the quality of the cohabitation after the wedding, whether it is internal, that is, of souls and minds, which is cohabitation in the principal idea; or whether it is only external...
